newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Fraud delays CLB 1996 earnings release to May.
newsitem.headline: Fraud delays CLB 1996 earnings release to May.

text.p: Credit Lyonnais Belgium (CLB), a unit of French Credit Lyonnais, said on Monday the release of its 1996 earnings report has been delayed until the end of May following news of a major fraud earlier this year.
CLB chief executive officer Philippe Cloes told Reuters that CLB's board would meet to review the report on May 23 and that the figures would be released shortly after.
Last year earnings had been released on April 17.
The bank said in March that a former employee had stolen 3.5 billion francs.
"The impact of the bank fraud on earnings will be limited. There will be no major surprise," Cloes said. "I hope earnings will be in the same order of magnitude as last year."
In March Cloes said the fraud would have no impact on 1996 earnings as it was covered by insurance.
CLB earned consolidated net profit of 628 million Belgian francs in 1995.
